answer: Fixture controls discriminate: a planted back-dated receipt is caught, a receipt completing before its catalog/event dependency is caught, a healthy ordered set produces zero inversions, and two timezone spellings of the same instant (2026-08-24T18:00:00Z vs 2026-08-24T14:00:00-04:00) are not flagged (UTC 2026-08-24T18:00:00Z) while naive civil comparison returns b_before_a. Clock-skew window is 2s; naive local-time comparison is forbidden. Production EVENTS.jsonl is present; git commit timestamps are NOT-CHECKED (no .git). Live receipts scanned=1048; clock-artifact rows=108 (declared ts vs mtime within skew or classified clock-artifact, not fabrication); missing declared ts=866; live causal inversions=148.

classification_policy.clock-artifact: mtime vs declared ts disagree on a tree where git and/or EVENTS.jsonl are absent; copy/rewrite/skew, not assumed fabrication
classification_policy.fabrication: UTC-aware causal impossibility beyond clock-skew, corroborated by event-log order, catalog dependency edges, or git commit time
classification_policy.unorderable-naive: timestamp lacks an offset; not compared as local civil time

question: Question: is any receipt causally impossible - written before the artifact it cites existed, before its dependency completed, or out of order relative to the append-only event log? Join EVENTS.jsonl against artifact mtimes and git commit times and flag every inversion. A back-dated receipt is either a clock artifact or a fabrication, and the two must be distinguished, not assumed.
residual_unknowns: Production append-only EVENTS.jsonl is absent, so live event-log order is NOT-CHECKED.
This worktree is not a git checkout, so live git commit timestamps are NOT-CHECKED.

reviewer.method: Re-derived ordering from fixture event logs alone (audit_event_log: no filesystem mtimes, no git).

tests.name: Known-broken control: planted back-dated receipt is caught
Timezone control: different offset spellings of one instant are not flagged
Dependency ordering: receipt completing before its dependency is flagged
Both-states: healthy ordered set produces zero inversions
Detector control: naive civil comparison would flag the timezone pair
Reviewer re-derives the same planted inversions from the event log alone

timezone_policy.dst_handling: compare UTC instants; DST does not invent inversions
timezone_policy.naive_timestamps: unorderable; never assigned the host local zone
timezone_policy.rule: Parse every timestamp to an aware UTC instant. Equal instants with different offset spellings are not inversions. Naive local-time comparison (strip tz, compare civil clocks) is forbidden because it manufactures inversions on this estate. DST is irrelevant once the comparison is on instants, not civil times.

title: Temporal integrity audit: detect back-dated or causally impossible receipts
